title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Marxist Film
description: Is Marx still useful in addressing social inequalities still prevalent in our times? This course aims to answer this question by examining a series of political films that attempt to challenge the logic of modern capitalism from a Marxist perspective.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Medical Imagination
description: Considers how films have mediated some of the most contentious and crucial dilemmas pertaining to health and the practice of medicine. Also explores the ways in which popular culture engages with the social and scientific contexts in which life and death decisions are made, as well as the anxieties about medical interference with biological limitations, from Frankenstein to Robocop, from monsters to cyborgs, from plagues to outbreaks.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Media and Violence
description: This seminar examines several of the issues related to representations of and discourses about violence in film and media. We begin with a consideration of the precursors to and emergence and consolidation of the so-called "ultraviolent" aesthetic (in the mid-to-late 1960s), then we consider a few of the film genres whose most prominent conventions include representations of violence (such as the gangster, horror, war, and boxing genres). In addition, the seminar includes a comparative approach to the issue of violent representations in film and media (especially television) by surveying the terms and themes that characterize both social scientific and humanities discourses.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Nazi Propaganda Film and Global Politics
description: Explores Nazi films role as an instrument for cultural diplomacy and propaganda in its historical and global political contexts. Topics include German-Japanese co-productions, German-American moviegoing, Nazi films in South America, worldwide competition with Allied films, and the films contemporary legacy.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Oil Culture
description: This seminar examines how our dependency on oil shapes modern ways of seeing and being. The course traces the media worlds of oil, from the origins of documentary film to contemporary contemplations of a world after oil.
